subject: Next steps: procurement path & PO vs card decision (ThermoData)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@thermodata.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@thermodata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: procurement path & PO vs card decision (ThermoData)

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has a clear view: 

Call summary (2 min):
- Use case: ThermoData wants Redwood for low-latency inference for their customer-facing feature (20–30k tokens/month to start).
- Key constraints raised: AP requires a PO for any vendor > $10k annually; SOC2 evidence required for onboarding; preference for vendor marketplace procurement if available.

Options to unblock (we can support all):
1) Card (corporate credit): fastest. We can onboard immediately once account owner adds card.
2) PO (net 30/45): Redwood accepts PO for annual or monthly invoices. For PO flow we need W-9, insurance cert, and signed MSA. Deliverables: quote + vendor onboarding checklist attached.
3) Marketplace (AWS Marketplace preferred): if ThermoData prefers, we can publish a private listing — this adds procurement-friendly billing but can take ~2–3 weeks to finalize.

Requested next steps from your side:
- Confirm preferred commercial path (card vs PO vs marketplace)
- If PO: share PO template / AP contact and expected cadence (monthly vs annual)
- If marketplace: confirm whether ThermoData has procurement admins who can accept listing terms

We'll attach a draft quote and the vendor-onboarding checklist. If useful, Karthik and I can put together an example PO invoice showing how charges will appear for AP.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-Options-commit-vs-payg.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet); vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@thermodata.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@thermodata.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement path & PO vs card decision (ThermoData)

Thanks Logan — helpful recap. A few clarifications from procurement/ops side: 

Quick answers:
- Our threshold: any vendor with annual spend > $10k must be on a PO. Early pilots expected to be ~8–12k/year depending on usage growth — close call.
- AP prefers annual POs but can do monthly if vendor invoices monthly and has a PO number. Net 30 is standard.
- Marketplace: preferred by procurement if available, because it preserves existing invoices and chargebacks.
- Vendor onboarding: we require W-9, proof of commercial general liability (COI), and SOC2 Type II report (or self-attestation + remediation plan).

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Can you accept a one-time pilot under card and then convert to PO if we exceed the $10k threshold?
2) How long does Redwood take to turn around a vendor onboarding checklist once we submit the documents?
3) Can you provide a line-item invoice example showing monthly charges vs annual commit?

Happy to loop procurement/AP folks if we have answers. I can share ThermoData's PO template if that helps.

-Elena
Director of Procurement | ThermoData Systems
elena.martin@thermodata.com | +1 617-555-0148

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Options / quick playbook for ThermoData PO vs Card

Logan — quick internal note to align on replies and attachments before I respond to Elena. Suggested playbook: 

1) Pilot on card, convert to PO if usage > $10k: we offer a 30-day conversion path. If they convert within 60 days we credit the card charges toward the first PO invoice (goodwill).
2) PO intake: request W-9 + COI + SOC2. We can provide SOC2 self-attestation immediately and share the latest Type II in 3–5 business days (if needed).
3) Marketplace route: offer to provision a private AWS Marketplace listing — timeline 10–18 business days to complete procurement paperwork + listing.
4) Pricing options: include monthly pay-as-you-go and a 12-month discounted committed tier (example in attached spreadsheet).

Attachments to include for external send: Redwood-Quote-ThermoData-20270922.pdf (formal quote), vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf. Internal: Redwood-Options-commit-vs-payg.xlsx (calc model).

Recommend we answer Elena's 3 questions directly and attach the sample invoice. I'll build the invoice template in the quote PDF.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement path & PO vs card decision (ThermoData)

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks for the fast response. Answers inline and attached: 

> 1) Can you accept a one-time pilot under card and then convert to PO if we exceed the $10k threshold?
Yes — we commonly run pilots on corporate card and convert to a PO for ongoing production. If you convert within 60 days we’ll credit the card charges against the first PO invoice.

> 2) How long does Redwood take to turn around a vendor onboarding checklist once we submit the documents?
Once we have W-9, COI and SOC2 (or self-attestation), onboarding usually takes 3–5 business days for our finance and legal teams to complete vendor setup. If you opt for marketplace billing it adds 10–18 business days for listing and legal review.

> 3) Can you provide a line-item invoice example showing monthly charges vs annual commit?
See attached quote (Redwood-Quote-ThermoData-20270922.pdf) — includes both PAYG (per-token billing by month) and a 12-month committed option with a 20% discount. Also attached: vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf.

Next practical steps: 
- If you want to pilot now: share the card or let us onboard one cardholder and we’ll spin up access by EOD.
- If you want PO: please send your PO template or AP contact and we’ll populate a first invoice and routing instructions (send POs to accounts@redwood.ai).
- If you prefer marketplace: confirm and we’ll start the private listing process (timeline ~2 weeks).

Link to HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-8342

Attachments: Redwood-Quote-ThermoData-20270922.pdf (PDF, 3 pages; includes sample invoice), vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Happy to hop on a quick 15-min call with AP if helpful.

Best —
